OpenAI Codex with GPT Image 2 as a free alternative to Claude Design
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI's updated Codex app now supports image generation via GPT Image 2, enabling a design-to-code workflow where it can generate visual concepts (dashboards, landing pages, UI mockups) and then code the interface. This is positioned as a free alternative to Anthropic's Claude Design, which requires a paid plan. GPT Image 2 is highlighted for its improved text rendering in images, making it useful for posters, infographics, and UI mockups.

recent_posts.title: How to use Claude Code with free and local model backends via a proxy
recent_posts.summary: A project called 'free-claude-code' lets you use the Claude Code CLI and VS Code extension without paying for Anthropic API usage by routing requests through a local proxy to alternative backends. Supported backends include NVIDIA NIM (recommended free option at 40 req/min), Open Router (many free models), DeepSeek, LM Studio, Llama.cpp, and Ollama. Setup involves installing the proxy, configuring a .env file with your chosen provider and API key, starting the proxy server on port 8082, and pointing Claude Code's ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to it. Advanced features include per-model mapping (routing Opus/Sonnet/Haiku tiers to different providers), smart rate limiting with exponential backoff, a model picker CLI, VS Code and JetBrains IDE integration, and Discord/Telegram bot support for remote agentic coding sessions with voice note transcription. The project has over 14,000 GitHub stars. Key caveat: output quality depends entirely on the backend model chosen, not Claude itself.

recent_posts.title: How to use DeepSeek V4 Pro and Flash for free via NVIDIA NIM APIs
recent_posts.summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4 Flash are now available via NVIDIA NIM APIs with free developer access through the NVIDIA developer program. DeepSeek V4 Pro is a 1.6 trillion parameter MoE model with a 1 million token context window suited for complex coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks. V4 Flash is a smaller 284B parameter model optimized for speed and lighter tasks. Both expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints at integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1, making them easy to integrate into tools like Cursor, Aider, OpenCode, and Codium CLI. The endpoints support a reasoning_effort parameter (none/high/max) to control thinking depth. Free access is intended for prototyping and development, not production workloads.

recent_posts.title: RooCode shuts down and Cursor may be acquired by SpaceX as AI coding tools consolidate
recent_posts.summary: RooCode is sunsetting its VS Code extension, cloud, and router on May 15th, while Cursor is reportedly being acquired by SpaceX (with a $60B option or $10B partnership deal tied to XAI). Kilo published two blog posts reacting to both events, positioning itself as the independent, model-agnostic alternative that stays committed to VS Code. The broader concern raised is AI coding tool consolidation: as model labs acquire or partner with coding tools, model flexibility for users may erode over time. The Windsurf/Anthropic precedent — where Claude access was cut when OpenAI acquisition rumors surfaced — is cited as a warning. The recommendation for developers is to keep workflows portable, prefer tools that allow model switching, and avoid lock-in to any single AI stack.

top_posts.title: Antigravity 3.0 adds custom skills, secure mode, and weekly rate limits
top_posts.summary: Antigravity 3.0 introduces three major updates: Skills (custom workflows triggered on-demand similar to Claude's code commands), revised rate limits (now weekly instead of 5-hour refresh for Pro users, though Ultra users remain unaffected), and Secure Mode (terminal permission controls with allow/deny lists). Skills enable team-shareable custom agent behaviors for tasks like code reviews and testing. The rate limit change disadvantages Pro tier users who may exhaust quotas faster, though access to models like Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro remains. Secure Mode addresses security vulnerabilities through configurable command execution permissions, from fully automatic to manual approval for each command.

top_posts.title: OpenAI Codex desktop app review and comparison with Conductor
top_posts.summary: OpenAI launched a desktop app for Codex (GPT-5.2), available free for a month and currently macOS-only. The app provides a graphical interface with features like skills, automations, and work trees, drawing comparisons to Conductor. However, the review highlights numerous UI/UX issues including inconsistent design, buggy interfaces, poor context handling, unintuitive controls (like the plan mode toggle), and problematic VS Code integration that spawns multiple instances. The reviewer suggests competitors like Verdant offer superior agentic interfaces despite OpenAI's resources.

top_posts.title: MiniMax M2.5 delivers near Opus performance at 30x lower cost
top_posts.summary: MiniMax M2.5 is a 230 billion parameter language model that delivers performance comparable to Claude Opus at 1/30th the cost. The model excels at agentic coding tasks, costs $1 per hour at 100 tokens/second, and successfully completed multiple complex development projects including Expo apps, Go terminal calculators, and full-stack web applications. Testing showed it performs particularly well in code generation workflows with planning mode enabled, completing tasks in minutes with proper error correction.

top_posts.title: How Claude's programmatic tool calling improves agent efficiency
top_posts.summary: Anthropic introduced Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC), a new capability in Claude Opus and Sonnet 4.6 that addresses a core inefficiency in agentic tool use. Traditional tool calling forces every intermediate result back into Claude's context window, creating latency and token bloat. PTC lets Claude write code that orchestrates multiple tool calls inside a sandboxed container, keeping intermediate results out of context and only returning the final processed output. This preserves the control surface of tool handlers (for logging, inspection, approval) while gaining the composability of code. Benchmarks show PTC improved accuracy by 11% and reduced input tokens by 24% on search tasks, helping Opus 4.6 reach #1 on LM Arena's search benchmark. PTC is now enabled by default when using the web search tool via the API.

top_posts.title: Claude Opus 4.6 with a design skill vs Google Stitch for shipping real UIs
top_posts.summary: A comparison of Google Stitch vs. using Claude Opus 4.6 with a front-end design skill inside the Verdant coding workflow for AI-assisted UI generation. The author argues that for shipping real production UIs, pairing Claude Opus 4.6 with a front-end design skill in Verdant is superior to Stitch, which is better suited for quick mockups and ideation. Key workflow tips include providing a visual thesis, content plan, and interaction thesis before building, using plan-first mode, and leveraging parallel workspaces to compare design directions in actual code.
